name: The Kano–Katsina wars

summary.text: Kano and Katsina, the two great market cities of Hausaland, fought over the trade routes for a century. Muhammad Rumfa's war with Katsina lasted eleven years and ended with neither side winning; Rumfa was the first Sarki to use the Dawakin Zaggi in it. His son Abdullahi and grandson Muhammad Kisoki fought a second war, again inconclusive, even as Kano conquered Zazzau. The rivalry outlived the wars: under Muhammad Zaki, Katsina harried a Kano weakened by Kwararafa, and the two only made peace around 1650, against Kwararafa.

moments.title: Rumfa's eleven-year war
moments.text: Kano's first war with Katsina lasts eleven years and ends inconclusively.

moments.title: Abdullahi and Kisoki's war
moments.text: A second war, fought by Rumfa's son and grandson, is also inconclusive.

moments.title: Peace against Kwararafa
moments.text: Kano and Katsina sign a treaty to face Kwararafa together.

reviewNotes: Katsina's own account of these wars (Usman 1981) has not been checked.
